title: Shielded Labs
description: Shielded Labs is an independent, donation funded Zcash support organization based in Switzerland. Its mission is to build unstoppable private money that…
text: Shielded Labs Shielded Labs is an independent, donation-funded Zcash support organization based in Switzerland. Its mission is to build unstoppable private money that empowers human freedom and self-sovereignty, with a focus on work that advances the sustainability, security, and scalability of the Zcash network. Shielded Labs adds independent engineering capacity to the Zcash ecosystem. It is not part of the Electric Coin Company, the Zcash Foundation, or Zcash Community Grants, and it describes itself as the first Zcash ecosystem organization that has not received direct or indirect funding from the Development Fund or block rewards. Mission and Role Shielded Labs focuses on protocol and infrastructure work that can make Zcash more resilient over the long term. Its public materials emphasize: Human freedom and financial privacy Independent funding outside the Development Fund Respect for ZEC holders and coinholder input User autonomy and self-sovereignty Technical innovation for sustainability, security, and scalability Collaboration with other Zcash contributors The organization contributes through direct engineering, public research, infrastructure support, and ecosystem coordination. It also maintains public resources for governance polling and coinholder-directed funding, helping Zcash community members understand when and how they can participate in governance signals. Current Projects Shielded Labs publicly lists several active project areas: Network Sustainability Mechanism - A set of proposed changes intended to support Zcash's long-term security budget while preserving the 21 million ZEC supply cap. The NSM work includes voluntary ZEC burns, issuance smoothing, and fee-burning proposals described in ZIPs 233, 234, and 235. Crosslink - A proposed hybrid consensus upgrade that would combine Zcash's proof-of-work block production with proof-of-stake finality, so ZEC holders could help secure the network while miners continue producing blocks. Dynamic Fees - Research and tooling for more predictable, user-friendly, and resilient Zcash transaction fees as the network evolves. Zero - A supported suite of open-source Zcash infrastructure software for exchanges, mining pools, wallet providers, and other organizations that rely on Zcash infrastructure. Ironwood - A Zcash network upgrade and shielded pool created in response to the Orchard counterfeiting vulnerability, designed to restore independently verifiable soundness of Zcash's circulating supply. Epoch - A research and engineering project announced in October 2026 to develop production-ready, high-assurance post-quantum cryptography for Zcash and expand formal verification of critical cryptographic components. The project targets a production-ready implementation by the end of 2027 that could form the basis of a future network upgrade. It complements Project Tachyon and other post-quantum efforts across the ecosystem. Epoch and cryptography team In October 2026 Shielded Labs launched Epoch, a dedicated effort to future-proof Zcash against quantum computing, AI-assisted attacks, and other advanced threats. The project aims to replace quantum-vulnerable cryptographic components and to apply formal verification to critical parts of the protocol. Epoch is led by a three-person cryptography team: Ulrich Haböck – Chief Cryptographer (formerly at StarkWare; earlier at Polygon Zero). Expert in zero-knowledge proofs and post-quantum cryptography; author of the logUp lookup argument and co-author of the Circle STARKs paper. Luke Edwards – Cryptography Engineer (formerly technical lead of the cryptography engineering team at Aztec). Holds a PhD in Applied Mathematics from the University of Arizona. Suyash Bagad – Cryptography Engineer (formerly at Aztec, working on the Barretenberg library and the PLONK family of proof systems). Holds BTech and MTech degrees from IIT Bombay; graduate research focused on privacy-preserving proofs of reserves. Phase 1 focuses on surveying existing research, evaluating candidate constructions against Zcash security and performance requirements, and producing a concrete post-quantum proposal. A production-ready implementation is targeted for the end of 2027. Ironwood Contribution In 2026, Shielded Labs played an important role in the ecosystem response to the Orchard counterfeiting vulnerability. The vulnerability was discovered by Shielded Labs security researcher Taylor Hornby and disclosed to Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL), which coordinated an emergency remediation with other Zcash contributors. After the emergency fix, the community still needed a way to restore independent confidence in Zcash's circulating supply. Ironwood addressed that by creating a new shielded pool using the corrected Orchard circuit and by sealing the original Orchard pool so funds could leave only through the turnstile. Shielded Labs worked alongside Project Tachyon, Valar Group, ZODL, and the Zcash Foundation on the design, review, and ecosystem preparation for Ironwood. This work demonstrated one of Shielded Labs' core roles in Zcash: adding independent protocol-development and security capacity outside the original Zcash development organizations. Governance Work Shielded Labs also publishes governance information for Zcash community members. Its governance page tracks protocol governance polls, ZCAP participation, coinholder-directed funding, and supported voting wallets. This helps make Zcash decision-making easier to follow for coinholders, ZCAP members, and broader community participants. Zcash does not use automatic on-chain governance for protocol changes. Polls and community input are advisory signals that feed into the broader rough-consensus process. Shielded Labs' governance work helps make those signals more accessible and easier to verify. Resources Shielded Labs website Shielded Labs projects Network Sustainability Mechanism Crosslink FAQ Dynamic Fees Zero Ironwood Epoch: Future-Proof Cryptography for Zcash Team Governance and polling Shielded Labs GitHub

title: Valar Group
description: Valar Group is an independent engineering organization focused on scaling Zcash, strengthening coinholder governance, and improving the privacy, performance…
text: Valar Group Visit website Mission Statement Valar Group is an independent engineering organization focused on scaling Zcash, strengthening coinholder governance, and improving the privacy, performance, and long-term resilience of the protocol. Its work is concentrated on protocol-level infrastructure: private token-holder voting, high-performance full-node software, wallet-sync technology, and network upgrades that make shielded Zcash more usable at larger scale. The organization aims to give ZEC holders a way to express preferences privately, give node operators faster and more capable software, and give wallets tools that preserve user privacy while reducing the cost of participating in the network. Background Valar Group is led by Dev Ojha (ValarDragon), a cofounder of Osmosis and a member of the team that launched Cosmos. Over the past decade he has worked across zk-SNARKs, BFT consensus, and production DeFi systems. The group’s public work in Zcash became prominent as the ecosystem shifted toward independent protocol teams after the 2026 reorganization of core development. Valar Group emerged as one of the organizations building the next generation of Zcash infrastructure alongside Project Tachyon, Shielded Labs, ZODL, and the Zcash Foundation. A recurring theme in its work is that Zcash’s privacy properties should extend beyond payments. If holders are asked to vote on issuance, block times, or network-upgrade scope, they should be able to do so from shielded balances without revealing identities, balances, or individual votes. That requirement led Valar Group to design and ship a dedicated coinholder voting chain. The same scaling and cryptography background also shaped its node and sync work. Faster blocks, lighter wallet synchronization, and a more capable full node are treated as prerequisites for private money that can be used at payment-network scale rather than only as a store of value. Vision Valar Group’s public materials and project work point toward a Zcash network that can: Support private, auditable coinholder voting as a repeatable governance process. Scale proof-of-work payments without sacrificing shielded privacy. Reduce wallet and node bottlenecks through PIR, pruning, and faster block propagation. Increase implementation diversity by shipping an independent full-node stack. Contribute to post-quantum readiness and formally reviewed protocol upgrades. The organization works as an independent contributor, not as a protocol owner. Protocol changes still move through ZIPs, implementation, review, and community signaling. Valar Group’s role is to design, implement, operate, and open-source the systems that make those processes practical. Strategic Areas Valar Group’s work clusters around four areas. Private Coinholder Governance Zcash does not use automatic on-chain protocol control. Coinholder polls are advisory signals that feed a broader rough-consensus process. Valar Group built the Tokenholder Voting Chain so those signals can be collected from shielded balances without exposing voter identity or individual vote size. The current design uses: A dedicated Cosmos SDK application chain to orchestrate voting rounds. Snapshot proofs against spendable Ironwood notes. Homomorphic encryption of vote amounts. Private Information Retrieval for nullifier non-membership proofs. A coordinator multisig and a distributed election authority. The goal is to replace earlier token-holder voting processes with a reusable, audited, wallet-integrable system that other organizations can operate and independently tally. Node Software and Network Scaling Valar Group collaborates with Project Tachyon on Zakura, a Zcash full node built from the Zebra codebase. Zakura is positioned as a high-performance node for operators who need faster initial sync, pruning, snapshot bootstrapping, and a compatibility path for former zcashd users. Related scaling work includes: Faster target block times, including 25-second block experiments on NU7 testnets. Improved peer-to-peer block propagation. Full-node features intended to keep Zcash usable as shielded activity grows. Wallet and Sync Infrastructure Shielded wallets historically have to scan large amounts of chain data. Valar Group develops PIR systems so wallets can fetch the proofs they need without downloading full nullifier sets or revealing which notes they care about. This work appears both in the voting stack and in broader wallet-sync research. The group has also contributed wallet-side reliability work, including multi-server transaction submission and server-selection improvements used in ZODL’s mobile stack. Protocol Upgrades and Ecosystem Coordination Valar Group was one of the organizations that publicly committed to the Ironwood response after the Orchard circuit vulnerability. Ironwood introduced a new shielded pool, sealed the original Orchard pool behind a turnstile, and restored a path to independently verifying circulating supply. Valar Group worked with Project Tachyon, Shielded Labs, ZODL, and the Zcash Foundation on architecture, consensus-rule implementation, and ecosystem coordination. The group also participates in NU7 scoping, testnet operation, and ZIP editing. Dev Ojha is listed as a ZIP editor. Current Initiatives Tokenholder Voting Chain / Shielded Vote Shielded Vote is Valar Group’s private governance protocol for Zcash. Holders vote with shielded balances without revealing individual amounts or linking votes to identities. Key properties include: One online session to vote, rather than a multi-day commit/reveal process. A Keystone-compatible snapshot signature that delegates voting rights to a hotkey without putting funds at risk. Encrypted vote amounts using homomorphic ElGamal. PIR queries so nullifiers are not leaked during snapshot proofs. Vote splitting and delayed relay submission to reduce timing correlation. Publicly auditable tallies. In August 2026, Valar Group and Project Tachyon used this stack for the NU7 coinholder vote. Eligibility required spendable shielded ZEC in Ironwood at mainnet height 3,459,350. Voting ran from August 25 through September 14, 2026, with a 1,000,000 ZEC participation threshold for the result to be treated as representative. Questions covered NSM issuance smoothing, reissuance timing, Sprout/v4 deprecation, 25-second block times, and NU7 scope/readiness. Default-chain coordination uses a 2-of-5 multisig among Project Tachyon, Valar Group, the Zcash Foundation, ZODL, and Shielded Labs. A separate validator set holds per-round decryption-key shares. No single validator can recover individual votes; a threshold of validators is required to produce the final tally. Public operator and auditor surfaces include: Voting chain setup Tally auditor Coordinator UI PIR server setup Shielded Vote documentation Zakura Zakura is a Zcash full node developed as a collaboration between Valar Group and Project Tachyon. It is derived from Zebra and adds faster sync, native pruning, snapshot bootstrapping, zcashd compatibility paths, and experimental high-performance P2P work. The Zcash Foundation publicly welcomed the project, noting that Zebra was released under permissive licenses so independent teams could fork and improve it, and that several Zakura contributors had already contributed upstream to Zebra. Private Information Retrieval Valar Group maintains PIR services and libraries for two related problems: Proving that a note was unspent at a snapshot height without revealing its nullifier. Reducing the data wallets must fetch in order to sync or vote. This is a core dependency of Shielded Vote and a building block for faster private wallet UX. Ironwood and NU7 Engineering Valar Group was part of the June 2026 joint commitment to Ironwood and contributed to consensus-rule implementation and client work around the new pool. It also operated NU7 testnet infrastructure, including join scripts and public nodes hosted under nu7.valargroup.dev. Open-Source Protocol Libraries The valargroup GitHub organization publishes the voting and node stack as public repositories, including: vote-sdk — application-specific chain for private on-chain voting zcashvoting — client-side shielded voting library, proofs, storage, and FFI voting-circuits — Halo2 delegation and vote circuits vote-nullifier-pir — PIR for nullifier non-membership proofs token-holder-voting-config — wallet service-discovery configuration zebra — Valar Group’s Zebra/Zakura development fork The Teams Valar Group is led by Dev Ojha (ValarDragon). Public team pages associated with Zakura list the following Valar-affiliated engineers: Dev Ojha — Maintainer; leads Valar Group. Focus areas include token-holder voting, post-quantum work, Zakura, and PIR. Roman Akhtariev — Principal engineer. Previously a principal engineer at Osmosis; work includes PIR wallet sync, token-holder voting, and Zakura sync performance. Evan Forbes — Principal engineer. Former Celestia consensus lead and founding engineer; work includes faster block-time readiness and a QUIC P2P stack. Adam Tucker — Principal engineer. Former Osmosis engineer; work includes token-holder voting with Roman Akhtariev, wallet reliability, and Ironwood integration across the stack. Zakura itself is maintained jointly with Project Tachyon, led by Sean Bowe. The two organizations collaborate closely but remain separate. Organizational Structure Valar Group operates as an independent engineering organization. It is not part of the Zcash Foundation, ZODL, Shielded Labs, or Zcash Community Grants. In the voting-chain design, Valar Group is one of five coordinator organizations. That role is a parameter of the voting system, not a claim of exclusive control over Zcash governance. Other teams can run validators, stand up alternative voting chains, or audit published tallies from the public tooling. Additional information about legal entity type, board composition, and internal governance has not been published in the same detail as older Zcash organizations. Funding Public forum statements from mid-2026 describe Valar Group and Project Tachyon as funded through private donations. Unlike ZODL’s disclosed venture round or Shielded Labs’ public donation announcements, Valar Group has not published a detailed donor list or grant schedule. That funding model keeps the team independent of the historic Development Fund / block-reward path, but it also means less public visibility into budget size and funding sources. Role in the Zcash Ecosystem Valar Group is one of the independent protocol organizations that formed around Zcash’s 2026 development landscape. In that landscape: The Zcash Foundation continues community stewardship and Zebra. ZODL focuses on wallet product and protocol continuation after the ECC split. Shielded Labs focuses on sustainability, security, and consensus research. Project Tachyon focuses on recursion, formal verification, and long-range scalability. Valar Group focuses on private coinholder voting, node performance, PIR, and the engineering required to operate those systems in production. Its distinctive contribution is making shielded governance operational. The NU7 vote is the first major use of that stack: holders prove Ironwood balances, wallets such as ZODL and Vizor can integrate the flow, and anyone can audit the tally without learning how a particular holder voted. The same team’s node and sync work is intended to support the other half of that picture. Private voting is less useful if wallets cannot sync, nodes cannot keep up, or upgrades cannot be implemented quickly. Valar Group treats governance, node software, and wallet infrastructure as one problem: make private Zcash usable at scale without concentrating operational power in a single organization. Resources Valar Group website Valar Group GitHub Shielded Vote documentation Voting chain setup Tally auditor Coordinator UI Zakura Zakura about / team NU7 coinholder vote forum thread Coinholder Voting Chain forum thread

title: Zcash Labs
description: Zcash Labs is an independent organization focused on the practical implementation, integration, and adoption of Zcash and its digital asset, ZEC. Zcash Labs…
text: Zcash Labs --- Zcash Labs is an independent organization focused on the practical implementation, integration, and adoption of Zcash and its digital asset, ZEC. Zcash Labs helps businesses, institutions, developers, and independent projects that want to use Zcash technology in products, services, payment systems, or applications that can be used in real-world scenarios. Zcash Labs positions itself as a go to market organization for Zcash. In the context of go to market, this means helping bring Zcash technology from existing technical capabilities to implementations that can be used by businesses and users. To achieve this goal, Zcash Labs combines consulting, solutions engineering, technical integration, infrastructure operations, product management, early-stage funding, financial underwriting, and co-marketing into a single approach oriented toward product launches and real-world use. Zcash Labs states that the organization is independent and not affiliated with the Zcash Foundation. This independent position allows Zcash Labs to determine on its own which projects, integrations, and infrastructure it wants to support using the resources and capital under the organization's responsibility. --- Background Zcash Labs was introduced to the public through its official website on August 6, 2026. On August 12, 2026, Zcash Labs then introduced its activities to the community through the Zcash Community Forum in an announcement titled Announcing Zcash Labs A Zcash Go To Market Company. Although the public announcement was made in August 2026, Zcash Labs states that its activities had been underway before that announcement. Zcash Labs had been working with projects that use Zcash and assisting in the development process before the Zcash Labs identity was widely introduced. One early example that was later announced to the public is its involvement in the development of zcashtocash. The emergence of Zcash Labs is related to the need to narrow the gap between available Zcash technology and the ability of businesses or developers to use it. A company may have needs that align with Zcash but not yet know the required technology, how to integrate, or the infrastructure to use. At the same time, a new project may have a promising concept but require technical assistance, product management, seed capital, or support to reach the production stage. Zcash Labs works in that space by providing support that connects business and developer needs with Zcash technology. Zcash Labs' approach begins with understanding the problem or needs of an organization. Once those needs are understood, Zcash Labs assesses whether Zcash is a suitable technology. If there is a match, Zcash Labs helps determine the technical approach that can be used to build the integration. This stage may include selecting available Zcash technologies, designing architecture, determining infrastructure requirements, and developing additional components if existing solutions are insufficient. With this approach, Zcash Labs can be involved from initial discussions about a use case to a system actually running. This forms the basis of Zcash Labs' position as an independent organization in the Zcash ecosystem that goes to market, because its work does not stop at planning or technical development, but also includes the process of bringing solutions to real-world use. --- The Main Purpose of Zcash Labs Zcash Labs’ primary goal is to drive broader adoption of Zcash by providing support that is immediately usable by service builders. This objective is pursued through several key avenues: helping businesses and institutions determine whether Zcash is suitable for their needs, assisting with the technical integration process, providing infrastructure support, and offering seed funding for projects with the potential to expand Zcash’s adoption. Zcash Labs aims not only to increase the number of projects using Zcash but also to lower the barriers to entry for those without in-depth technical experience. To that end, they offer a comprehensive process that begins with consultation, followed by strategy development, technical implementation, and, if the project is deemed promising, funding support. --- Zcash Labs' Main Areas of Work According to its official website, Zcash Labs lists four main ways it supports the use of Zcash. First, it provides consulting and advice to assess whether Zcash aligns with an organization’s business or operational needs. Second, they provide technical support and implementation solutions for institutions that are currently integrating or planning to integrate Zcash. Third, they distribute seed grants and assist with co-marketing coordination so that projects can reach the right audience. Fourth, they implement a “coinholder retroactive grants” approach, which involves covering project costs upfront and then seeking reimbursement through a coinholder-based grant process. According to an announcement from the Zcash Community Forum, the organization’s initial focus is more specifically described as the integration of the Zcash blockchain for businesses and institutions, the operation of independent infrastructure services, and support for new projects that expand the practical use of Zcash. This explanation demonstrates that Zcash Labs operates at the intersection of technical development, market needs, and ecosystem growth. --- How Zcash Labs Works with Partners and User Candidates Zcash Labs explains a fairly simple workflow. The process begins by understanding the needs of those who approach them, then honestly assessing whether Zcash is indeed suitable for that use case. If it is, they help map out the usage flow, technical requirements, and various trade-offs or design implications that need to be considered. After that, they can assist in building the technical solution and, where relevant, help with funding and co-marketing activities. This approach is important because not every project is automatically a good fit for Zcash. By placing the assessment phase at the beginning, Zcash Labs strives to be a pragmatic implementation partner, rather than merely an adoption advocate that ignores the fit with real-world needs. --- Infrastructure Operations by Zcash Labs In addition to facilitating third-party integrations, Zcash Labs also operates and develops the infrastructure that supports access to the Zcash network. When it was introduced to the public, the organization stated that it operates a Shielded Vote Validator and is developing services that include a Zcash full node, lightwalletd, and RPC infrastructure. Full nodes are used to connect directly to the network and verify blockchain data. lightwalletd helps wallets and lightweight applications retrieve the necessary data from the network without running the entire blockchain locally. Meanwhile, RPC provides a way for external software to communicate with blockchain nodes or services. Operating this infrastructure is directly tied to Zcash Labs’ integration efforts. Businesses and developers building Zcash applications require reliable access to the network. By running these services independently, Zcash Labs can expand the range of available infrastructure options while gaining firsthand experience with the technical requirements of the integrations it facilitates. Zcash Labs also stated that additional RPC services will be developed as its infrastructure grows. This indicates that Zcash Labs’ activities are not only focused on building applications on top of Zcash, but also on providing the technical infrastructure that enables those applications or projects to communicate with the Zcash network. --- Support for the Zcash Project Zcash Labs supports independent projects deemed to have the potential to expand the use of Zcash. Support can be provided from the early stages, when a project is still just a concept and does not yet have all the resources needed to begin development. In this process, Zcash Labs can help determine the technical direction, manage product development, address integration needs, provide infrastructure, and offer seed funding. The goal is to help a team move from the idea stage to a usable product. In a public discussion on the Zcash Community Forum, Zcash Labs stated that initial funding for startups in the early stages of organizational activity generally ranges from 5 to 10 ZEC. This amount is not a fixed limit, as Zcash Labs also considers larger funding amounts for integrations deemed to have strategic value for the adoption of Zcash. This approach allows Zcash Labs to be more proactive in seeking out opportunities it deems beneficial. Zcash Labs does not have to wait for a project to secure funding before providing assistance, as some of the work can be funded using Zcash Labs’ own capital. --- Funding Model and Business Approach from Zcash Labs --- Funding Model One of Zcash Labs’ key characteristics is its use of an upfront funding model. Under this approach, the organization can fund projects in advance using its own capital, so a team does not always have to wait for the grant process to be completed before beginning product development. This funding can be used for new projects, business and institutional integrations, infrastructure development, and co-marketing activities. Zcash Labs determines on its own whether a project is deemed compelling enough to receive initial funding. Since these decisions involve capital for which the organization is responsible, Zcash Labs bears the financial consequences of the choices made. Once the work is completed and has produced something that can be evaluated, Zcash Labs can submit the expenses incurred through the Coinholder Directed Retroactive Grants mechanism. Thus, providing capital to builders and deciding on reimbursement are two separate processes that occur at different times. In the retroactive grants mechanism, a project is evaluated after the work has produced something that can be reviewed. Zcash Labs first provides funding to support development, then submits the results of that work to ZEC coinholders. Zcash Labs explained that reimbursement requests are intended to cover expenses already incurred plus a 20 percent markup. This additional amount serves as compensation for the financial risk and operational work undertaken by the organization while supporting the project. For example, if Zcash Labs uses $5,000 in capital to fund a project, the organization can submit a request for $6,000 based on this model. The $5,000 represents the initial costs, and the $1,000 is the additional 20 percent compensation. Such reimbursement requests are not automatically approved. Coinholders decide whether the work produced is deemed valuable enough to warrant funding. If a request is denied, the capital already spent remains the responsibility of Zcash Labs. --- Risk and Financial Underwriting Since reimbursement is not guaranteed, Zcash Labs acts as a financial underwriter. In this context, a financial underwriter is a party willing to provide capital and bear the financial uncertainty upfront so that a project can begin. Builders who receive support do not have to bear the entire risk while waiting for the results of retroactive funding. They can receive payments based on the agreed-upon work, while Zcash Labs assumes the risk of whether those expenses will eventually be reimbursed. This structure creates an incentive for Zcash Labs to be cautious when selecting projects. Zcash Labs must consider whether a product has a clear use case, is feasible, has the potential for adoption, and provides benefits that can be assessed by ZEC holders. If that assessment is inaccurate and reimbursement is denied, Zcash Labs bears the financial consequences of that decision. --- Project Selection and Development Zcash Labs doesn’t just wait for projects to come to them seeking funding. Zcash Labs can also identify issues it deems important, seek out teams or developers capable of providing solutions, and then provide support if the proposed approach is deemed viable. This approach is evident in Zcash Labs’ public activity on X. Zcash Labs once sought solutions to a bug bounty issue in the development of artificial intelligence and stated that funding was available for solutions deemed capable of resolving the problem. This approach gives Zcash Labs a more active role in ecosystem development. Zcash Labs can identify needs early on, determine whether those needs are relevant, find suitable builders, and then use capital to help solutions reach the implementation stage. --- Business Approach, Equity, and Ownership Zcash Labs’ initial model differs from that of traditional venture capital firms. In a discussion on the Zcash Community Forum, Zcash Labs stated that it has not taken equity in the projects it has supported. The team is generally paid based on agreed-upon work or deliverables. Thus, receiving funding from Zcash Labs does not automatically make the organization a partial owner of a project. Zcash Labs also stated that equity is not the primary mechanism they use to align interests with the projects they support. If Zcash Labs were to make an equity investment in the future, the organization stated that the cost of acquiring that equity would not be reimbursed through a retroactive grant. Any relevant ownership relationships would also be disclosed should such a situation arise. --- ZcashToCash ZcashToCash is one of the earliest projects publicly known to have received support from Zcash Labs. The project was created to help users convert ZEC into fiat currency through peer-to-peer transactions. zcashtocash uses infrastructure from Peer. This system is used to verify fiat payments before ZEC is released in a transaction. When Zcash Labs was introduced to the public, the service already supported Cash App, Chime, Monzo, Revolut, Venmo, and Zelle. According to information provided when the project was announced, this combination of payment services offers the potential to cover more than 100 geographic regions. The team also plans to expand the number of supported payment apps and regions. Zcash Labs had been working with the zcashtocash team prior to the project’s launch. Its involvement included funding as well as technical and product management support. As a result, zcashtocash became one of the first examples demonstrating how Zcash Labs combines capital, product development, and implementation support within a Zcash project. In this case, Zcash Labs helped move an idea toward implementation, provided the necessary resources during development, and used the completed results as the basis for applying for retroactive reimbursement. --- Product Management Product management is another aspect of the support Zcash Labs provides to projects. This function helps a team define product requirements, set development priorities, bridge the gap between user needs and technical implementation, and ensure the project progresses toward a launch-ready product. This role complements solutions engineering. Solutions engineering focuses on how to solve a technical problem, while product management helps ensure that the solution built aligns with the product’s goals and reaches users. The combination of the two allows Zcash Labs to operate not merely as a software development team, but as an organization that helps a project navigate the process from idea to a fully operational product. --- Co Marketing Zcash Labs also provides co-marketing for certain projects. Co-marketing is a joint marketing effort aimed at helping existing products reach relevant users. This activity is part of the go-to-market approach because the success of an integration is not determined solely by the software’s ability to function. A product also needs to gain distribution, be discovered by the right users, and have a path to real-world adoption. By incorporating co-marketing into its support model, Zcash Labs can remain involved even after the technical development phase is complete. The organization can help projects transition from the development phase to the adoption phase. --- The Relationship with ZEC Coinholders In the Zcash Labs model, the organization and ZEC coinholders have distinct roles. Zcash Labs determines whether it is willing to take on the risk of providing capital to a project, while coinholders determine whether the results produced warrant retroactive reimbursement. This separation allows development to begin without first obtaining coinholder approval. Zcash Labs can make decisions based on internal assessments and use its capital to carry out the work. Once verifiable results are available, coinholders have the opportunity to assess whether the work has provided sufficient value. In this way, coinholders do not determine which projects Zcash Labs may initiate. They determine whether the work that has been completed is eligible for reimbursement through the retroactive funding mechanism. --- The Independence of Zcash Labs Zcash Labs has publicly stated that it is an independent organization and is not affiliated with the Zcash Foundation. Decisions regarding which projects to support are made by Zcash Labs, and the funds used are under the organization’s responsibility. Zcash Labs therefore does not operate as a committee that allocates funds belonging to the Zcash Foundation. Interaction with the community funding mechanism occurs after the work is completed, when the organization can submit a request for retroactive reimbursement to coinholders. This structure allows Zcash Labs to act independently when selecting projects and experimenting with new approaches, while still receiving economic feedback from ZEC holders regarding the work that has been completed. --- The Importance of Zcash Labs in the Ecosystem Zcash Labs’ role can be understood as a bridge between Zcash technology and the practical needs of adoption. Many blockchain projects have robust technology but struggle to achieve widespread adoption due to integration barriers, a lack of technical support, or uncertainty regarding initial funding. Zcash Labs aims to fill that gap by offering a more agile combination of consulting, implementation, infrastructure, and funding. If their model succeeds, Zcash Labs could serve as an example of how an independent organization can drive Zcash adoption through incentives directly tied to the coinholders’ community’s assessment. Therefore, Zcash Labs is important not only as a service provider but also as an organizational experiment in the financing and growth of the Zcash ecosystem. --- Directions for Development When the organization was introduced to the public, Zcash Labs stated that there were additional projects and integrations in the works but not yet announced. Information regarding this work is planned to be released gradually as each project is ready to be introduced. In the area of infrastructure, Zcash Labs also plans to expand available services by providing additional RPCs. In terms of funding, the organization is starting with relatively small grants while observing how coinholders respond to requests for retroactive reimbursement. If this model gains traction, Zcash Labs may increase the amount of capital deployed and take on risk in larger projects or integrations. These developments could include support for more businesses, startups, infrastructure, and services that use Zcash. As of August 2026, Zcash Labs is still in the early stages of its public activities, so the number of projects, integrations, and infrastructure is still growing. --- Public Outreach Zcash Labs uses zcashlabs.org as its main website to explain its services, funding model, projects, and organizational developments. More detailed information about its funding approach is also published on a dedicated page about the funding model and in organizational announcement articles. Zcash Labs also uses the Zcash Community Forum to discuss with the community how the organization operates. Announcement threads provide additional explanations regarding the size of initial grants, financial underwriting, reimbursement risks, the approach to equity, and plans to scale up activities if the model gains support. On social media, the organization uses the @ZcashLabs account on X to publish updates, projects, funding opportunities, and needs for solutions deemed relevant to Zcash. --- Summary Zcash Labs is an independent organization focused on Zcash’s go-to-market strategy, integration, and practical adoption. Zcash Labs helps businesses, institutions, developers, and independent projects use Zcash technology to build products, services, and infrastructure that can be used in the real world. The Zcash Labs model combines technical expertise with funding. The organization can help design and build integrations, provide infrastructure, manage product development, and use its own capital to support work before receiving reimbursement. Once a project produces something of value, Zcash Labs can submit a request for reimbursement through the Coinholder Directed Retroactive Grants mechanism, with a 20 percent markup added as compensation for risk and operational expenses. If the request is not approved, the financial risk remains with Zcash Labs. Through this approach, Zcash Labs aims to create a more direct path from a need or idea to a fully functional and usable Zcash implementation. --- References Zcash Labs Announcing Zcash Labs: A Zcash Go-to-Market Company Zcash Labs on X Zcash Labs on GitHub Zcash Labs on Web Blogs

title: Coinholder-Directed Retroactive Grants
description: The Coinholder Directed Retroactive Grants Program funds completed work that has delivered verifiable value to the Zcash ecosystem.
text: Coinholder-Directed Retroactive Grants The Coinholder-Directed Retroactive Grants Program funds completed work that has delivered verifiable value to the Zcash ecosystem. It draws from the Coinholder-Controlled Fund (12% of block rewards + Deferred Dev Fund Lockbox seed), established by ZIP 1016 and activated in NU6.1 (November 2025). The program runs quarterly until the 3rd halving (2028). Funds are held in multisig by Key-Holder Organizations (e.g., Shielded Labs, FPF). --- Grants are retroactive only - rewarding past contributions (e.g., development, integrations, community building). Prospective work should apply to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG, 8% of rewards). --- Eligible Applications Focus: Completed, publicly verifiable work benefiting Zcash (privacy, adoption, tooling, security). Criteria (coinholders evaluate): Demonstrated impact and delivered value. Alignment with Zcash values (privacy, decentralization). Transparent evidence (code, reports, metrics). No restrictions: Anyone (individuals, teams, organizations) can apply or be nominated. Competing proposals: Voted separately; highest ZEC support wins. Veto possible: By Key-Holders for legal issues or harm to users/community (rare, with rationale). How to Submit an Application Prepare Proposal: Describe completed work, impact, evidence (links, deliverables). Specify requested amount (ZEC/USD equivalent) and justification. Include payout address and contact. Submit: Post on Zcash Community Forum (forum.zcashcommunity.com) in the Grants section. Title: "[Retroactive Grant] - [Project Name]". Use clear markdown format. Deadline: Quarterly; announced on forum/X (e.g., Q4 2025: October 12, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC). Late submissions: Resubmit next round or apply to ZCG. Engage: Respond to community questions during 30-day review. note: Administered by FPF (compliance, communication); proposals compiled on GitHub for visibility. Voting Process and Cadence Quarterly Cadence (e.g., Q4 2025, Q1 2026): Submission Deadline: Mid-quarter (announced). 30-Day Review: Starts post-deadline; discuss/feedback in forum threads (summary thread often created). Voting Period: Follows review (e.g., 1-2 weeks in November for Q4). Results & Disbursement: Soon after; approved grants paid per terms (KYC for >$50k). Voting: Coinholders vote with ZEC holdings (no lockup; Orchard pool eligible). Mechanism: Decentralized polling (e.g., via voting authorities). Approval: at least 420,000 ZEC quorum + simple majority yes. Independent votes; coins reusable across proposals. Public, transparent results. note: Current Round (as of January 5, 2026): Q4 2025 completed (November vote); Q1 2026 submissions expected soon - monitor forum for announcements. Latest Updates: Check the Zcash Community Forum Grants Section. Process may evolve with community feedback.

title: Sovright
description: Sovright is a US 501(c3) non profit dedicated to supporting human autonomy. Starting with a focus on Zcash infrastructure, mining, protocol development, and…
text: Sovright Sovright is a US 501(c3) non-profit dedicated to supporting human autonomy. Starting with a focus on Zcash infrastructure, mining, protocol development, and ecosystem support the project builds tools and services intended to strengthen private digital currency infrastructure and support the long-term resilience of the Zcash network. Sovright was previously known as Bootstrap. The original name reflected the organizations early goal of bootstrapping a Zcash infrastructure company from the ground up. Visit site Name The name Sovright is a compound of sovereign and right. It reflects the organizations focus on individual sovereignty, privacy, and the right to choose how personal data, money, communications, compute, and online activity are controlled. Sovrights work began with Zcash, a privacy-preserving cryptocurrency that uses zero-knowledge cryptography to support shielded transactions. Over time, the organizations focus expanded beyond private money to include broader infrastructure concerns, including secure communications, resilient networks, private compute, and secure AI interactions. Mining Pool Sovright operates a Zcash mining pool at: mining.sovright.com The Sovright Mining Pool is designed to support miner sovereignty and reduce mining pool concentration. Mining pool concentration is a recurring concern in proof-of-work networks because a small number of pools can end up controlling a large share of network hashrate. This can weaken decentralization and increase reliance on the behavior of major pool operators. The Sovright Mining Pool is intended for solo miners, small operators, and other participants who want to support a more decentralized Zcash mining ecosystem. The pool emphasizes transparent payout logic, auditability, and minimal operational fees. The current testnet version does not provide payouts and is intended for testing only. (Coming Soon) Network Resilience Network resilience refers to the reliability and robustness of the infrastructure that carries Zcash transactions. Private transactions depend not only on cryptography, but also on the availability and reliability of the network infrastructure beneath them. Sovright identifies network resilience as a foundational area of work for maintaining the practical security and usability of Zcash. Financial Sovereignty Financial sovereignty refers to the ability of individuals to control and access their own funds without relying on permission from intermediaries. In the context of Zcash, this includes private payments, self-custody, and infrastructure that allows users to transact on their own terms. Sovright treats financial access and user-controlled money as core components of individual sovereignty.

title: Obscura Labs
description: Obscura Labs is an independent organization registered in Nigeria with a strategic focus on Africa and other emerging markets.
text: Obscura Labs Visit website Mission Statement Obscura Labs is an independent organization registered in Nigeria with a strategic focus on Africa and other emerging markets. Its mission is to build infrastructure, tools, and practical adoption pathways that improve the accessibility, utility, decentralization, and long-term resilience of the Zcash ecosystem across Africa. The organization aims to support the use of privacy-preserving financial technology by improving access to reliable infrastructure, supporting developers and businesses, educating users, and strengthening local Zcash communities. Background Obscura Labs was founded by Chidi Olisa, the lead of Zcash Nigeria. Before establishing Obscura Labs, Chidi contributed to the Zcash ecosystem through community building, education, advocacy, localized content creation, user support, and initiatives designed to introduce people in Nigeria and other parts of Africa to financial privacy and Zcash. Engagement with users, students, developers, businesses, and community members highlighted several barriers to broader Zcash adoption across Africa. These included limited infrastructure, difficulty accessing ZEC through local currencies, insufficient developer support, a shortage of localized educational resources, and limited integration with everyday payment systems. Obscura Labs was created in response to these challenges. The organization is based on the view that awareness alone is not sufficient for sustainable adoption. Communities also require reliable infrastructure, accessible products, developer tools, financial access, education, and long-term institutional support. Vision Obscura Labs vision is to help make Africa one of the strongest regions for Zcash infrastructure, adoption, and ecosystem growth. The organization aspires to become a leading African contributor to the Zcash ecosystem by: Operating reliable Zcash infrastructure. Improving access to ZEC and privacy-preserving payments. Supporting users, developers, businesses, and community organizations. Building practical tools and services. Encouraging the development of sustainable Zcash communities. Increasing the geographic diversity of Zcash infrastructure and ecosystem participation. Strategic Areas Obscura Labs initially plans to focus its work across four strategic areas. Infrastructure Development Reliable infrastructure is necessary for wallets, applications, developers, exchanges, payment services, and users to interact with the Zcash network. Obscura Labs operates and develops Zcash infrastructure within Africa to improve network accessibility, geographic diversity, reliability, and resilience. This work is intended to reduce reliance on a small number of infrastructure operators and provide dependable services for users and developers in African markets. Infrastructure initiatives may include: Public Zcash mainnet RPC endpoints. Public Zcash testnet RPC endpoints. Zebra full nodes. lightwalletd services. DNS seeders. Public infrastructure monitoring. Developer-focused APIs. Integration tools and documentation. Additional services that reduce the barriers to building on Zcash. By making infrastructure more accessible, Obscura Labs aims to support developers, wallets, applications, businesses, and services integrating with the Zcash ecosystem. Adoption and Financial Access For Zcash to be useful in everyday situations, people must be able to acquire, store, use, and exchange ZEC without unnecessary friction. Obscura Labs supports initiatives intended to improve: Access between ZEC and African local currencies. Fiat on-ramps and off-ramps. Merchant adoption. Payment integrations. Cross-border payments. User onboarding. Wallet accessibility. Practical use of ZEC by individuals and businesses. Particular attention is given to services that address challenges commonly experienced in African markets, including currency instability, financial exclusion, expensive cross-border transfers, limited access to global payment systems, and increasing financial surveillance. Community Growth and Awareness Obscura Labs supports the development of sustainable Zcash communities throughout Africa. Its community initiatives may include: Educational workshops. University outreach. Community events. Localized content. Translations. Developer training. User onboarding. Ecosystem partnerships. Contributor development programs. Support for regional Zcash communities. The organizations objective is not limited to increasing general awareness. It also seeks to help communities develop the knowledge and resources needed to educate users, support local adoption, train developers, and produce future advocates and ecosystem contributors. Ecosystem Collaboration Obscura Labs works with organizations, developers, educators, researchers, businesses, infrastructure operators, and community leaders throughout the Zcash ecosystem. This collaboration is intended to support initiatives that: Advance financial privacy. Strengthen the Zcash network. Improve the usability of ZEC. Expand access to Zcash infrastructure. Encourage open-source development. Support emerging Zcash communities. Increase ecosystem participation from Africa and other emerging markets. Obscura Labs operates independently while working toward shared objectives with other Zcash ecosystem participants. Current Initiatives Although Obscura Labs is in an early stage of development, several initiatives have already begun. African DNS Seeder Infrastructure Obscura Labs operates DNS seeder infrastructure from Africa. DNS seeders help new Zcash nodes discover peers when connecting to the network. Increasing the geographic distribution of seeders contributes to the decentralization and resilience of the Zcash peer-to-peer network. Zebra Node Infrastructure The organization operates Zebra nodes within Africa. Zebra is an independent implementation of the Zcash consensus protocol. Operating Zebra infrastructure contributes to network accessibility, implementation diversity, and the geographic distribution of Zcash nodes. lightwalletd Services Obscura Labs operates lightwalletd infrastructure to support Zcash wallet connectivity. lightwalletd provides blockchain data to light-client wallets without requiring each wallet user to operate a complete Zcash node. Reliable lightwalletd services are therefore important for mobile wallets and other lightweight Zcash applications. Infrastructure Monitoring Obscura Labs is developing public monitoring and status systems for its infrastructure. These systems are intended to improve operational transparency by allowing users and developers to check the availability and status of publicly accessible services. ZecFiat ZecFiat is an Obscura Labs initiative focused on improving access between ZEC and African local currencies. The project is intended to reduce barriers for individuals and businesses seeking to acquire, use, or exchange ZEC. Its broader objective is to make Zcash more practical within markets where access to cryptocurrency services and international financial systems may be limited. Further information about ZecFiat’s structure, supported markets, availability, and operating model is expected as the initiative develops. The Teams Obscura Labs was founded by Chidi Olisa, who also leads the Zcash Nigeria community and Gentle Fox is an infrastructure engineer and contributor at Obscura Labs, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and reliability of the organization's infrastructure and services. The organization is currently in its early development stage. As it grows, Obscura Labs intends to establish a small team of part-time contributors with experience in areas including: Infrastructure operations. Software and product development. Education. Community development. Business and payment integrations. Ecosystem support. Communications. Governance and organizational operations. Obscura Labs is also engaging experienced professionals, industry experts, and Zcash ecosystem contributors who may provide strategic guidance or serve as advisors and board members. Organizational Structure Obscura Labs is an independent organization registered in Nigeria. The organization is being developed with a focus on establishing the governance, expertise, and operational capacity required to support sustainable growth and long-term contributions to the Zcash ecosystem. Its planned organizational structure may include: A founder and executive leadership. A small operational team. Part-time technical and community contributors. A board or equivalent governing body. Independent advisors. Partnerships with ecosystem organizations and local communities. Additional information regarding its governance structure, legal status, board membership, and organizational policies may be published as the organization develops. Funding At launch, Obscura Labs is expected to be funded primarily through: Donations. Strategic partnerships. Grants. Ecosystem-aligned funding opportunities. Support for specific infrastructure, product, or community initiatives. Initial funding will be used to support infrastructure operations, product development, community initiatives, organizational expenses, and the recruitment of contributors. Over time, Obscura Labs intends to develop a sustainable funding model that allows it to consistently deliver measurable value to the Zcash ecosystem while maintaining its independence. Role in the Zcash Ecosystem Obscura Labs is part of a growing group of independent organizations contributing to Zcash through infrastructure, software development, education, community support, and adoption initiatives. Its work is intended to increase geographic and organizational diversity within the ecosystem by establishing additional Zcash infrastructure and development capacity in Africa. The organization’s activities contribute to several broader ecosystem objectives: Improving the decentralization of Zcash infrastructure. Increasing access to Zcash services in underserved regions. Supporting the development of local technical expertise. Expanding the number of independent ecosystem contributors. Improving access to privacy-preserving financial technology. Supporting practical ZEC adoption by users and businesses.

title: ZingoLabs
description: ZingoLabs is a team of visionaries dedicated to enhancing the human experience. We believe that technology should benefit humanity and that we thrive through…
text: ZingoLabs Official Website - GitHub - X/Twitter - Instagram ZingoLabs is a team of visionaries dedicated to enhancing the human experience. We believe that technology should benefit humanity and that we thrive through consensual interactions. We are identifying the patterns that make this possible. Zingo Lab Cyan operates as a Shielded DAO. We store our funds in a treasury where every member has a view key. Funds are spent from the treasury when members vote in favor of a proposal. Projects Zingo! Wallet (GitHub) Zingo Wallet is a fully featured Zcash wallet designed for user friendliness, although it includes some advanced features for more advanced users. It supports transparent, Sapling and Ironwood pools, has an address book for recurrent payments and is available in various languages. It was the first wallet to support Orchard and to implement NU5 formats. One of the main features of Zingo! is its ability to use the Memo field to offer valuable insights about your transactions. Zingo! is available for mobile devices and PCs. You will find all downloads here Zingolib (GitHub) An API and test-app that exposes zcash functionality for app consumption. Zingolib provides both a library for zingo-mobile, as well as an included cli application called zingo-cli, a command-line light wallet that talks to a chain indexer such as Zaino. Zaino Indexer (GitHub) Zaino is a Rust indexer for the Zcash blockchain, developed by the Zingo team. It is the indexer in the Z3 stack: it indexes chain data from a Zebra validator and serves wallets, explorers, and other clients. It is the successor path to lightwalletd. Zaino offers essential features for both light clients, such as wallets and applications that do not require the full blockchain history, and full clients or wallets. It also supports block explorers, granting access to both the finalized blockchain and the non-finalized best chain and mempool managed by a Zebra full validator. zcashd reached its End-of-Support halt on 18 July 2026 at block 3,417,100 and does not support Ironwood (NU6.3). Zaino reads a Zebra validator. ZLN (zcash-local-net) (GitHub) A set of utilities that launch and manage Zcash processes. This is used for integration testing in the development of: lightclients indexers validators Its goal is to offer a highly adaptable and sturdy testing environment for core nodes (validators) such as Zebra, indexers like Zaino, and light client wallets such as zingo-cli. The default stack it launches is Zebrad, zainod, and zcash-devtool. The legacy zcashd and lightwalletd processes sit behind an unsupported legacy-stack feature and are scheduled for removal. In addition to providing tools to start, cache, and load Zcash chain data (for mainnet, testnet, and regtest), zcash-local-net is used from Zaino's test suite to assess the Lightwallet RPC services hosted in Zaino (see Zaino testing docs).

title: ZKAV Club
description: Supported by The Zcash Foundation this ambitious grassroots project aims to have global impact through local and regional actions. Inviting a community of…
text: ZKAV Club Website - GitHub - X/Twitter - YouTube Supported by The Zcash Foundation this ambitious grassroots project aims to have global impact through local and regional actions. Inviting a community of creators to learn and work together to elevate and disseminate news and stories that inspire, educate, and share the promise of Zcash and financial privacy. Mission Statement We are a global collective of content creators who care about privacy, Zcash, and building community. Together we will build a space to share information, skills and resources to aid production and publishing of content that covers the topics we care about. We want stories told by the people who are closest to the action, sharing their passion and lived experiences to bring privacy education and Zcash to every part of the world. The long-term goal of the Zk Av Club is to establish a network of capable, ready and funded media producers to broadcast and share news about Zcash and privacy that is both locally relevant and globally consumed. Collaboration & Partnerships The Zk Av Club will host regular online meetups and collaborate with local events to facilitate discussions on topics of interest to the global Zcash and privacy communities. With our focus on online audio/visual production this will be the time and place to learn more about the media needs and concerns of local Zcash and privacy-focused communities around the world and to take action. Events Events will be open and free, and could include many formats such as presentations, Q+A, AMA, workshops, troubleshooting, brainstorming or something else entirely. Every discussion, no matter which format, will maintain the Zcash focus on privacy as a topic and as a practice. Consent cannot be assumed. Who We are a global community of voices and experiences. Through community we will empower and amplify every individual to tell the Zcash story through their own perspective, on their own terms. We will foster resources and connections that motivate and support content creators so they can bring their unique voice to the global privacy conversation. We envision a web of connections speaking and creating in different languages, all feeding off of, and contributing to, the information and content shared by the Zk Av Club. We will lift each other up and together we will build the momentum needed to bring Zcash and privacy to the world. Join us! Everyone is invited and welcome to be a part of the Zk Av Club! Anyone with a passion for privacy who is interested in exploring new audio/visual and internet technology can attend meetups and participate to the degree of their own comfort. title: Community Broadcasting using VDO.Ninja and OBS Studio
description: This short tutorial was created during the DWeb Camp 2023 by group of fellows and volunteers. The goal of this exercise is to leverage on using smart phone…
text: Community Broadcasting using VDO.Ninja and OBS Studio This short tutorial was created during the DWeb Camp 2023 by group of fellows and volunteers. The goal of this exercise is to leverage on using smart phone devices connected to offline MESH network for collaborative video recording and streaming. We use two open source software OBS Studio (Open Broadcaster software) and VDO.Ninja. These software could be downloaded and run locally on your computer. OBS Studio (Open Boardcaster software) OBS Studio is Free and Open source software for recording and live streaming that is available for multiple operating systems. The software was first released in 2012 and enjoys quite a large following among game streaming community and independent video content creators. The OBS Studio user interfaces could look quite daunting for the first the time users. The OBS studio is divided into two windows "Preview" and "Broadcast". The preview window shows available videos (various cameras such as webcam, Iriun Webcam, OBS Virtual Camera, Video and Browser source) called "Scenes" and "Broadcast" shows the live stream. In order to stream from a remote camera stream from VDO.ninja into OBS Studio, you start by adding a new "Browser Source" with "Sources > Add > Browser". In the new window, you can provide the source URL from VDO.Ninja and select "Make source visible". Now you can now start broadcasting the remote streams. VDO.Ninja VDO.Ninja is an Free and open source web application that allows you to turn your mobile devices into live streaming camera. The software could downloaded and deployed onto your local computer or you can directly use the online version at https://vdo.ninja. The VOD.Ninja interface is simple, just open the VDO.Ninja in your mobile devices web browser and select "Add your camera to OBS". You'll then select your camera and audio device from list of devices and click "Start". You'll then get "view" link which can add to OBS Studio. Directing a community call with VDO.Ninja Start by going to VDO.ninja with your web browser on a desktop/laptop. To create a new room and direct your own community call livestream, click Create a Room. The next screen will ask for basic information to setup your room. Once a room is created, the director has a lot of control options available on the following screen. When people join your room then you, the director, will see all of the source options and controls appear with their video and audio. FAQ What types of video graphic cards are required for OBS Studio ? You can use a personal computer with good graphic card and lots of memory or alternatively you can use a hardware encoders Teradek VidiU Does OBS allow you to do live translation and captioning? There are some community contributed plugins that seems to be provide such a feature. https://github.com/eddieoz/OBS-live-translation Could you develop your own plugins for OBS Studio? Yes, OBS has support lua, python scripting. Also JavaScript for Overlays and webviews. Do we use live fade to black or transitions? That is up to you, the producer! Is there a latency when you are streaming? This depends mostly on the destination to where you are streaming. For example, YouTube might have a delay of a minute or more due to video processing that is done on their servers before being broadcast. Audio drops when using OBS on slow machine and while doing green-screening Use Hardware encoder or use stream yard https://support.streamyard.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056350852-How-to-Use-OBS-Virtual-Camera-with-StreamYard or RiverSide.FM Credits Ryan Ajay Arky Resources https://obsproject.com/help https://docs.vdo.ninja/ Office Hours: The media and digital event community https://alex4d.com/notes/item/media-and-digital-event-community

title: Publish a Site on IPFS
description: IPFS (InterPlanetary File System) is a peer to peer protocol and network designed to create a decentralised method of storing and sharing files.
text: Publish a Site on IPFS Introduction to IPFS IPFS (InterPlanetary File System) is a peer-to-peer protocol and network designed to create a decentralised method of storing and sharing files. Unlike the traditional client-server model of the internet, IPFS allows users to share files directly with each other, rather than relying on a centralised server to store and distribute content. Files in IPFS are addressed using content-addressing, meaning each file is given a unique hash or CONTENT IDENTIFIER (CID) based on its content, and this hash is used to retrieve the file from the network. When a user adds a file to IPFS, the file is broken up into small pieces called blocks, and each block is given a CID. These blocks are then stored on different nodes in the network, so that the file can be easily retrieved from multiple sources. This ensures redundancy and fault-tolerance while also making it difficult for any one node to become a single point of failure or control. Read: An Introduction to IPFS Creating your Site For this example we are creating a simple website. Example Site Step 1: If you are unfamiliar with web design write the main content for your website including Title, Main Body of text, with links to other pages/site & footers. Step 2: Use a HTML template! Paste the text you have written accordingly. Optional to also create a .CSS stylesheet for your website. Step 3: Save your directory. All .html pages + images must be in the same Folder. Setting up a Node Download and install IPFS from the Official website. Initialise IPFS: If you are using the Desktop Application you will not have to initialise. Using a Terminal or command prompt, Run command: ipfs init Add Site Folder to IPFS: Select the folder with your website files and navigate to the Add Folder option. – If using Terminal, Run command: ipfs add -r foldername to add the entire folder recursively to IPFS. Pin Site on IPFS: Once your website files are added to IPFS, you need to pin them to ensure they remain available on the network. – If using Terminal, Run command: If using Terminal, Run command: ipfs pin add hash hash = CID of the folder you added in the previous step. Alternatively, you are also able to pin directories using services such as Pinata or Dolpin It saves a lot of time! – Access your website on IPFS: Your website is now published on IPFS and can be accessed using the hash of the folder. To access your website, you can visit https://ipfs.io/ipfs/hash hash = CID of the folder. In our case the CID = QmW2UEfap1vrRRvS5H9wed8qmsx4WsvXBk3GPGVVfWx3r3 IPNS Interplanetary Naming System (IPNS) allows you to update the IPFS CIDs associated with your website and still serve a static link. It is provided as a key. In the settings menu for your site folder on IPFS desktop application select Publish to IPNS. Key: “k51qzi5uqu5di670a6uxywo17b2be1eyhoa2cl0qlwpfxn5p9ypcu8jbzgnj4n” It can also be used to view our site via a gateway: https://ipfs.io/ipns/k51qzi5uqu5di670a6uxywo17b2be1eyhoa2cl0qlwpfxn5p9ypcu8jbzgnj4n DNS Link The site has been created, now we need a way to point a URL to the content. If you already own a web address you are able to add a new record using the TXT record dnslink(your domain). Depending on provider it may auto populate. It will take time to propagate through the network before you can view it. Congratulations! You now have a censorship resistant website. Resources IPFS Documentation IPNS Documentation DNS link Docs

title: Serve GitHub Repo with IPFS
description: In this guide we learn how to create a git cloneable URL for your GitHub repository served using an IPFS CID.
text: Serve GitHub Repo with IPFS Introduction In this guide we learn how to create a git cloneable URL for your GitHub repository served using an IPFS CID. This is useful to ensure content availability regardless of geographic region, censorship resistance and as a persistent backup of valuable information! Note: Data uploaded to IPFS is available to all network users. You may wish to locally encrypt personal/sensitive data. Install IPFS Kubo Follow installation instructions provided here In this example we use Linux, other OS versions are available. Check installation was successful using ipfs –version Clone Repository To start, select a Git repository you want to host & clone it: Run Command: “git clone https://github.com/zechub/zechub” Now, to get it ready to be cloned via IPFS. cd zechub git update-server-info Unpack Gits objects: Doing this will allow IPFS to deduplicate objects if you update the Git repository later on. Add to IPFS Once you have done that, that repository is ready to be served. All that is left to do is to add it to IPFS: $ pwd /code/myrepo $ ipfs add -r The resulting CID: Qmbgqox5g3614gjTb43s5mdSmmk95aGWWA9EHksL2T91A2 Brilliant! Now your repository is uploaded to the network. Clone using IPFS You should now be able to retrieve the GitHub repository using: git clone http://ipfs.io/ipfs/yourCID Alternatively you are able to search & retrieve using your local IPFS node. Final Note: The repo folder on IPFS does not receive updates alongside the actual github repository. It is recommended to reupload the folder at regular intervals.
